A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CRANE paper with complete, readable main text and appendices. Text comparison, rendered-page inspection, and matching figure images support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CRANE experiments on GSM-Symbolic and FOLIO, including benchmark comparisons, few-shot ablations, and sampling comparisons in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original GSM-Symbolic and FOLIO experiments and their main-text and appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same delimiter-triggered switching between unconstrained reasoning and constrained generation. No algorithm components, inputs, or procedures change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same GSM-Symbolic expression-generation task and FOLIO natural-language-to-first-order-logic task. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GSM-Symbolic uses unconstrained generation with and without CoT and IterGen constrained generation; FOLIO uses unconstrained CoT and SynCode constrained generation. The appendix sampling comparators also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The model sets, prompts, metrics, and decoding settings are unchanged, including the 600/800-token limits, main 8-shot/2-shot setups, 203-instance FOLIO validation split, and appendix temperature-0.7 sampling.

E4.justification: Both retain the same few-shot analysis in Figure 3 and Table 3, GSM-Symbolic case study in Appendix C.3, and sampling comparisons in Appendix C.4 and Tables 4–5.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The three-sample pass@1/2/3 reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5, Figure 3, and the qualitative examples report identical results. For example, CRANE's GSM-Symbolic accuracy with Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct remains 38%, and its FOLIO accuracy with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct remains 46.31%.

T1.justification: The definitions, expressivity assumptions, Propositions 3.1 and 3.3, Lemma 3.2, and supporting material in Appendices A–C are unchanged. Equation movement reflects page reflow only.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about restrictive grammars reducing expressivity, grammar augmentation preserving reasoning, and CRANE outperforming the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: The interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the finite-language restriction of Proposition 3.1 and CRANE's dependence on access to model output logits.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same hardware, PyTorch/Transformers implementation, decoder libraries, prompt templates, and grammars. No implementation or code/data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 6, the cited works, and the reference list are unchanged. The distinction from grammar-aligned decoding and prior expressivity research remains the same.

P1.justification: The first-page proceedings/copyright notice is replaced by 'Preliminary work' and an ICML under-review/do-not-distribute notice; the arXiv version/date stamp also changes. The scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter first-page notice produces small text and figure-placement shifts across pages 1–8. Figures and tables retain their content and design; pages 9–22, including all appendices, render identically.

improvement.justification: The changed publication notice and minor page reflow leave the method, proofs, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations unchanged. The PDFs therefore establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
